title: Smallest square room
prompt:
Floor tiles are 1 m by 1 m. Write a function `square_side(area)` that returns the side, in whole metres, of the smallest square room that can hold a floor of `area` square metres. Use `math.sqrt()` and `math.ceil()`.

For example, `square_side(30)` returns `6`, because 5 m is too small (25 m2) and 6 m is enough (36 m2). The result must be an integer.

hints: The side of a square with area `a` is the square root of `a`, but a fraction of a metre isn't enough, so round up.
`math.sqrt` gives a float; `math.ceil` rounds up and returns an int.
